research_question: Using only the preceding two minutes of routine ADS-B state, which causal current-state information stably predicts newly arising geometric proximity interactions over the next 30, 120, and 300 seconds across unseen source days and a second airport?
claim_boundary: Prediction of an ADS-B-derived geometric interaction proxy; not controller workload, an official loss of separation, accident probability, or universal airspace complexity.

primary_target.episode_rule: Count one onset when a pair is inactive at cutoff and enters the joint horizontal/vertical proximity state in (cutoff, cutoff+horizon]; after clearing, a later re-entry is a new onset.
primary_target.future_observation_rule: Both aircraft must have post-cutoff reports no older than the frozen staleness bound at a future grid time.

model_policy: Low-capacity models only, fixed random seed 1701, identical rows/splits/features within each comparison, and training-day-only preprocessing.

metrics.uncertainty: paired source-day bootstrap and exact two-sided sign test

confirmation.selection_rule: Mechanically select unused dates by predeclared year/season strata and authenticated row count without reading scene targets or model outputs.

stopping_rules: If future-onset performance loses useful signal after persistence and exposure controls, narrow the claim to persistence/nowcasting and do not imply prospective conflict emergence prediction.
If neither B nor C improves on A at at least two of three horizons under equal-day primary metrics, stop representation expansion and do not add a GNN or Transformer.
Do not retune after the one-shot KBTP confirmation or add another KBTP confirmation batch.
If the frozen KBTP scheme needs KAGC-specific tuning or materially reverses, retain a KBTP-only claim.
